title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 2:47
body: “But let us look again, if it seem good to you, at the words of the jailor, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" What language sweeter than this?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 3:1
body: “Let us learn not to sink under affliction, nor to repine; for look at this blessed saint. He had been scourged, and sorely scourged, for it is said, "When they had laid many stripes upon them." He had been bound too, and that again sorely, for the jailor cast him into the inner ward, and with extraordinary security.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 3:21
body: “And observe, I pray you, herein also the lowly-mindedness of Paul. For though he were in peril because of the Gospel he preached; yet saith he not, he was saved for his merit, but for the mercies of God.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 4:2
body: “Again, observe also the piety of the Children: they showed no indignation, no anger, no gain-saying, but they came forth. Had they regarded it as an act of vengeance that they had been thrown into the furnace, they would have been grieved against the man who had cast them in; as it is, there is nothing of the kind; but, as though they were going forth from Heaven itself, so went they forth.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 4:27
body: “Now to this end God hath opened to us many ways. For, "Tell thou first," saith He, "thy sins, that thou mayest be justified" ( Isa.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 7:9
body: “But why does he call it "old?" Either because our former life was of this sort, or because that which is old is "ready to vanish away," (Heb.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 7:14
body: “Here, give heed to me carefully, and see that no part escape you of what I say. For our contest is with enemies : wherefore we first must practice the reductio ad absurdum which also Paul often doeth.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Daniel 12:2
body: “Again, he touches the point of the Resurrection, since this was the most encouraging hope to the hearer, and gave him a security from what had happened unto Christ. Now be not thou afraid because thou art compassed about with a dead body.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans
